newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia shares end lower as gold stocks continue tumble.
newsitem.headline: Australia shares end lower as gold stocks continue tumble.

text.p: Australian shares closed lower on Monday, led by declines in the gold sector and other resource stocks but trade was quiet as many players waited for U.S. markets to re-open after the July 4 holiday.
"This has been a long and gloomy day," one dealer said.
The All Ordinaries index ended 20.4 points down at 2,713.0 with about A$550 million (US$410 million).
The gold sector index plummeted another 6.8 percent after losing 4.1 percent on Friday.

Last week's news that the Reserve Bank of Australia had sold two thirds of its gold reserve in the past six months has seriously hurt gold stocks and fuelled the already dramatic recent price fall in gold bullion, dealers said.

"It just seems to be getting worse as the days go by...I think it is going to be a while before the prices of our major gold stocks get back to reasonable figures again," said Kevin Lourey of Peake Lands Kirwan in Melbourne.
Australia's largest listed gold miner Normandy Mining lost nine cents to A$1.32 as investors seemed to ignore optimistic comments on earnings from the group earlier on Monday.
Market heavyweight Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, was the biggest faller amongst the blue-chips, losing 35 cents to A$19.25.
